title: Bouncing ball

caveats: motion blur visible during fast fall

reference.basis: ten alternating black-white segments typical of a 1 m metre stick with 10 cm divisions

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, narration or visual indication of slow motion; motion appears real-time

subjects.description: small round yellow ball that falls, bounces and rolls

observation.what_happens: A small yellow ball drops from below a striped scale near the top left and falls toward the brown floor while drifting rightward, bouncing twice. The motion starts at release under the scale and ends with the ball rolling to the right along the floor.

calibration.note: black and white striped bar = 1 m (ten alternating black-white segments typical of a 1 m metre stick with 10 cm divisions) spans 485 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: black and white striped bar = 1 m (ten alternating black-white segments typical of a 1 m metre stick with 10 cm divisions) spans 485 px in SAM's mask, known to ±30%
reasoning: The y data shows repeated fall-rise arcs with falling peak heights and near-constant rightward drift, classic for gravity flight plus two inelastic floor bounces. Apparent free-fall acceleration is low for the 1-m scale, suggesting scale error up to 30% and possible air drag on a light ball. Candidates therefore compete vacuum flight against linear and quadratic air drag, all with a restitution bounce event and floor level to predict the unseen settling to rolling.

critique.finding: The ball drops under gravity with g = {g} and rebounds from the floor at {floor_y}. Each bounce keeps {e} of its vertical speed.
critique.headline: The ball falls freely; the air barely touches it.
critique.why_it_won: It lets the ball bounce off the floor while the plain projectile cannot, and it skips air drag that does nothing for this short fall.

headline: The ball falls freely; the air barely touches it.
finding: The ball drops under gravity with g = 6.2 ± 1.9 m/s2 and rebounds from the floor at -0.97 ± 0.29 m. Each bounce keeps 0.74948 ± 0.00020 of its vertical speed.

eyeball.law_in_words: Projectile in free fall with constant vertical gravity g and constant horizontal velocity, bouncing on a horizontal floor at y=floor_y with normal restitution e = outgoing/incoming vertical speed.
